variants.name: Branching tree
variants.prompt: Create one polished desktop WEBSITE DESIGN MOCKUP for Shoulders, an editorial interactive explainer of software foundations. Landscape 1536x1024, a finished interface screenshot, not a moodboard, not a poster. Crisp original PIXEL ART integrated with beautifully typeset real UI text. Body typography must be readable, headings strong and substantial, never thin. No generic SaaS dashboards, badges, permanent sidebars, pricing, search or accounts. Show the SAME researched example across alternatives: VS Code depends directly on Electron, xterm.js, ripgrep; Electron contains Chromium and Node.js; Node.js uses V8. Do not imply xterm.js or ripgrep depends on Electron. User has SELECTED Node.js. Include a legible selected-component explanation with exact concise text: "Node.js" / "JavaScript outside the browser" / "Provides: a runtime and system APIs." / "VS Code adds: the editor, debugging and extension experience." / "Use directly: build and maintain your own application." Links "Explore V8 →" and "View evidence ↗". Include small scope sentence "Desktop VS Code · Illustrative scale, not a measure of fragility." Show product identity and a breadcrumb "Explorations / VS Code". Illustration labels and interface text should look like semantic UI overlays, not text painted onto objects. Convey a plausible selected state and a next action. No stock photography, 3D realism, watercolor, or stone-arch buildings. DIRECTION A — BRANCHING TREE. Small visible top label "A / Branching tree". Quiet natural-history field guide meets pixel-art engineering schematic. Light almost-white paper, deep pine-green active path, warm ochre secondary highlights, charcoal text. Typography: strong humanist sans headline, mono small labels. Composition: small Shoulders wordmark upper left, breadcrumb and bold headline "Follow the roots of VS Code." Then a spacious orderly actual dependency TREE drawn with crisp stepped pixel branches and compact hand-crafted pixel-art object nodes, not floating circles. VS Code is a substantial editor workstation at top center. Three clearly independent descending branches end at Electron runtime console, xterm.js terminal, ripgrep search toolbox. Only Electron branches again to Chromium and Node.js. Node.js selected in green, its V8 child is shown on the active path. Tree is the main visual across 65% of canvas; the selected Node explanation is an attached generous inline reading panel in the lower-right white space with an elbow leader clearly linked to the selected Node, without occluding anything. Restrained and wonderfully clear; no excessive foliage. Small bottom hint "Open a branch to go deeper." Clear hierarchy with varied node sizes, no endless sprawling network.

Small visible top label "B / Small supports, big tools". An original witty editorial pixel-art engineering drawing inspired by the IDEA of surprisingly large systems standing on small foundations; do not reproduce any existing comic. Warm cream paper, black bold condensed sans headings, brick-red active labels. Headline "Big tools. Small foundations." A large elevated VS Code editor workspace, drawn like an oversized pixel-art workshop platform with monitor, extension drawers and debugging controls, rests on three visually separate supports. Electron is a large left runtime plinth; xterm.js is a small but clearly readable central terminal module; ripgrep is a tiny sturdy right search toolbox. Clear relationship lines establish each supports VS Code, no danger/cracks/collapse. Electron's own foundation splits visibly to two modules Chromium and Node.js below it; Node.js is selected with red frame. Do not make one tiny support seem like the sole dependency. Generous asymmetrical poster-like whitespace; pixel structure on the right two-thirds, headline on left upper third. A broad editorial explanation strip across the bottom contains the selected Node.js text in three readable columns (provides / product adds / use directly), with Explore V8 and evidence links. Hand-drawn-looking straight rules but pixel artwork only. Memorable, intelligible, slightly playful, no dense UI. Small caption "Support size is illustrative."

Slightly game-like discovery, not a game HUD. Show only a manageable visible slice with a slim depth marker beside each stratum.
